name: Arbitron API
description:
Funding rates, executable cross-venue spreads and the listings calendar across the perpetual futures venues Arbitron tracks. Read-only JSON over HTTPS. API and MCP access are part of every Arbitron plan: see [the plans](https://arbitron.app/developers#plans).

## Authentication

Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer arb_live_...` (the `X-Api-Key` header is accepted too). Create one at https://arbitron.app/settings/api; it is shown once. MCP clients can sign in with an Arbitron account through OAuth 2.1 instead of a key.

## Rate limits

Each key has a minute window and a month window, sized by its plan. Both are advertised on every response in the IETF `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` fields, so a client can pace itself and never see a `429`. For example:

```http
RateLimit-Policy: "minute";q=120;w=60, "month";q=100000;w=2592000
RateLimit: "minute";r=118;t=41, "month";r=87500;t=1209600
```

`q` is the quota for the window, `w` its length in seconds, `r` the requests left and `t` the seconds until it resets.

- A spent window answers `429` with `Retry-After` in seconds and a problem body naming the window.
- The month resets on the 1st at 00:00 UTC. Quotas are hard caps; nothing is ever billed as overage.
- One request is one request: history, spreads and funding cost the same, and an MCP tool call counts like a REST call.

## Caching

Every data response carries an `ETag`. Send it back as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged body answers `304`, which is refunded on both windows. `Cache-Control` is `private, max-age=15` on live data and `max-age=300` on delayed data, matching how often the snapshot behind it moves.

## Errors

Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`): `type`, `title`, `status`, a `detail` that says what to change, the request id as `instance`, a stable `code`, and `suggestions` where a close match exists. `type` is `https://arbitron.app/developers/errors#<code>`, and every code is explained at [https://arbitron.app/developers/errors](https://arbitron.app/developers/errors).

## Versioning

`/api/v1` is the contract. Fields, endpoints, enum values and optional parameters are added without a version change. Removing or renaming anything, changing a type or changing a default is v2, and v1 keeps working for twelve months after v2 ships. A deprecated endpoint or field announces itself with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers and a `Link` to the changelog entry that names the replacement. The MCP server follows the same version, and tool names never change within a major version.

### Changelog

- **2026-09-20** v1 published: funding, funding history, spreads, listings, exchanges, coins and usage. MCP server with eight tools, key or OAuth.
